sentences.text: By this award, the claim petition bearing MACP No. 291/22 filed on behalf of the petitioners Jyoti Verma & her children (i.e. legal heirs of deceased/victim Vijay Kumar) seeking compensation under Sections 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, arising out of the accident, would be decided.

2. Briefly stated, the facts mentioned in the claim petition are that on 05.03.2022, the deceased namely Vijay Kumar was returning to his home at Delhi alognwtih other family members, including Petitioner No.1, on a tempo traveller bearing Registration No. UP-14GT-7958 after darshan of Vaishno Devi Shrine and at about 04:30 A.M., when he reached near Patti Kalyana, GT Road,
Village- Shamlkha, Panipat, Haryana.

While driving the said tempo traveller, offending vehicle bearing Registration No.HR-63C-1352, which was coming from back side and being driven in a rash,
negligent and zigzag manner, suddenly changed lane and came in front of vehicle of the deceased and applied brakes without any indication and hit against the offending vehicle.
As a result, the deceased was crushed in the vehicle and received fatal injuries as per MLC and post-mortem Report.
He was shifted to Government Hospital and declared dead and further post-mortem on his body was conducted.
Accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by R1.

In connection with the said accident, an FIR bearing No. 156/22 dated 05.03.2022 PS Samalkha,
District- Panipat, Haryana, u/s 279/304-A was registered against the driver of the vehicle bearing Registration No. HR-63C-1352.

During investigation, it was found out by police that the _____________________________________________________________ offending vehicle is being driven by Respondent No.1.
3.
In response to the notice of petition, counsel for R3 appeared.

R1 & R2 did not choose to appear and file written statement and no WS was filed on behalf of R3/Insurer either and hence,
opportunity to file Written Statement was closed on 11.12.2023.
However, later on application moved by R3 seeking recalling of the said order, the application was allowed and Written Statement filed by Respondent No.3 was taken on record.

Respondent No.3 /New India Assurance Company Ltd. has stated that deceased was responsible for accident as per the contents of FIR itself, as he did not maintain safe distance from the vehicle moving ahead of it and dashed against it and further complete documents are not filed with the claim petition.
Other general defences have been taken and Insurer has denied the averments made in the petition.

4. Upon completion of pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed vide order dated 11.12.2023:-
i).

Whether Mr. Vijay Kumar (deceased), husband of Petitioner No.1 and fathers of petitioner Nos. 2 & 3 died in a motor vehicular accident that occurred on 05.03.2022 at about 04:30 am near Patti Kalyana, GT Road, Village Samalka, within jurisdiction of PS Samalka due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration No.
HR-63C-1352 driven by respondent No.1 / Pradeep Kumar?

5(i).

PW1/petitioner No.1 namely Jyoti Verma tendered her evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/1 and deposed regarding the offending vehicle being driven in a manner as suddenly being turned and coming in front of the victim vehicle and driver applying brake without any indication and vehicle being driven at a very high speed and resulting in accident due to sudden applying of brakes and resulting in fatal injuries to the husband of PW1.

She relied upon the following documents:-
 Photocopies of aadhar card of petitioner, her son Amit Verma and deceased Vijay Kumar @ Vijay Verma are collectively Ex.PW1/A and Aadhar card of her son Sumit Verma is Mark A.
Driving Licence of deceased victim Sh. Vijay Kumar is Ex.PW1/B.
No education related document of deceased has been filed on record.

6.

7. I have heard the final arguments advanced by Ms. Sulekha Thakur, Learned counsel for the petitioners and Sh. Arvind Kumar, Learned counsel for respondent No.3/ insurer.
I have perused the evidence and other materials placed on record.

It is pertinent to mention here that as per settled proposition of law, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

Even the insurance company has not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.
11.
FIR was lodged on the complaint given by petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased Jyoti Verma on the next date of the accident.

It was alleged in the complaint to police that at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle was moving ahead of the victim vehicle and being driven at a fast speed and in a wrongful manner, which made the occupants in the victim vehicle think that driver of the offending vehicle was drunk.

Hence, the driver of the victim vehicle i.e. husband of Jyoti Verma started overtaking the offending vehicle with a view to escape from the same (bachkar aage nikalne lage) but the driver of the offending vehicle suddenly turned his vehicle, resulting in collusion of victim vehicle with offending vehicle and the offending vehicle moving ahead of the victim vehicle stopped and victim vehicle also stopped due to being entangled in the offending vehicle (Hamari gaadi bhi usme fas ke band ho gayi).
It is seen that the manner of accident as mentioned in the claim petition filed by the petitioner is remarkably different from the version in the FIR.

It is mentioned in the claim petition that on the date and time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle came from back side while driving his vehicle in a rash, negligent and zigzag manner and suddenly changed lane and came in front of the deceased/victim vehicle and applied brakes without any i n d i c a t i o n a n d h i t a g a i n s t t h e o f f e n d i n g v e h i c l e r e s u l t i n g i n _____________________________________________________________ deceased being crushed in the victim vehicle.
In support of the claim petition, petitioners have examined P1 Jyoti Verma as a witness.

She deposed on the lines of the claim petition and testified that the offending vehicle was suddenly turned and came in front of victim vehicle and brake was applied on the offending vehicle without any indication and further that the driver was rash, negligent and driving at a very high speed.

During her cross-examination, PW1 stated that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving in a zigzag manner and changing lanes frequently & at the time of accident and he first overtook the victim vehicle and came ahead of the victim vehicle and then suddenly applied brakes, due to which the deceased could not control the victim vehicle and hit against the open body offending vehicle.
She also deposed that the offending vehicle was being driven at different speeds and sometimes it was being driven fast and sometimes slow.

From a bare reading of the FIR, which contains the earliest version of the accident from the eyewitness/PW1 Jyoti Verma, it is clear that the offending vehicle had stopped only after the collusion and not prior to it and the stand taken in the claim petition regarding sudden putting of brakes on the offending vehicle resulting in the accident is clearly an improvement over the earlier version and cannot be Jyoti Verma vs Pradeep Kumar on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157115972/
4 readily bought.
However, petitioner is consistent in her testimony on the point of the offending truck having been turned in a negligent manner resulting in the accident.
This version is consistent with the complaint given to the police, on which FIR is based.

Hence, it is clear that the offending vehicle was not being driven in a proper manner and further, the same was being driven in a wrong m a n n e r , a s e x p l a i n e d b y p e t i t i o n e r N o . 1 i n h e r _____________________________________________________________ cross-examination, where it is stated that the offending vehicle was being driven in a zigzag manner and the driver was changing lanes frequently.

Further, irrespective of whether it was the deceased in the process of overtaking the offending vehicle or the offending vehicle having come ahead of/in front of the victim vehicle from back side, sudden turning of the vehicle towards the victim's vehicle itself points out the negligence of the offending vehicle.
It is further seen that at the time of the accident there was hardly a gap of half feet between the offending vehicle and the victim vehicle.

It is not the plea taken by the petitioners that the victim vehicle was in the process of overtaking the offending vehicle and hence, there was little gap between the two vehicles and on the other hand, the stand taken by the petitioners is that the offending vehicle had come in front of the victim vehicle and applied sudden brakes.

As discussed, the alleged factum of sudden putting of brakes is inconsistent with the FIR and informant is none other than the petitioner herself and she has not averred a word to dispute the facts stated in the FIR.

Hence, once she has relied on the FIR,
irrespective of the fact that she was not confronted with the FIR during her cross-examination, the facts stated therein cannot be completely ignored.

It is clear that it was the duty of deceased injured as well to maintain safe distance from the vehicle moving ahead of it on the road and had the deceased been careful, the accident if not averted, at least the magnitude of impact could have been avoided.

Hence, some contributory negligence on the part of the deceased is also evident but as largely the accident took place due to the negligent driving by R1, who did not take care of the vehicle coming from behind, by taking a sudden turn, I am of the considered view that _____________________________________________________________ contributory negligence to be attributed to the deceased is only 10 per cent.

12. Thus, in view of the above, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners have been able to prove that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred largely due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into fatal injuries to the deceased victim Vijay Verma.
Therefore, issue no.1 is decided partly in favour of petitioners.

ISSUE No.2 13. In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, after deduction towards contributory negligence, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 14. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and Jyoti Verma vs Pradeep Kumar on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157115972/
5 reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
15. The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
_____________________________________________________________ "Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.
So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned

,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future;
(ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience,
discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
16. In Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

The relevant paragraphs of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered _____________________________________________________________ as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn Jyoti Verma vs Pradeep Kumar on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157115972/
6 as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general  damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of  prospects of marriage)
( v i ) L o s s o f e x p e c t a t i o n o f l i f e ( s h o r t e n i n g _____________________________________________________________ of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.
It is not the plea taken by the petitioners that the victim vehicle was in the process of overtaking the offending vehicle and hence, there was little gap between the two vehicles and on the other hand, the stand taken by the petitioners is that the offending vehicle had come in front of the victim vehicle and applied sudden brakes.
As discussed, the alleged factum of sudden putting of brakes is inconsistent with the FIR and informant is none other than the petitioner herself and she has not averred a word to dispute the facts stated in the FIR.
Hence, once she has relied on the FIR,
irrespective of the fact that she was not confronted with the FIR during her cross-examination, the facts stated therein cannot be completely ignored.
It is clear that it was the duty of deceased injured as well to maintain safe distance from the vehicle moving ahead of it on the road and had the deceased been careful, the accident if not averted, at least the magnitude of impact could have been avoided.
Hence, some contributory negligence on the part of the deceased is also evident but as largely the accident took place due to the negligent driving by R1, who did not take care of the vehicle coming from behind, by taking a sudden turn, I am of the considered view that _____________________________________________________________ contributory negligence to be attributed to the deceased is only 10 per cent.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
15. The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.
16. In Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
17.
Hence, his income has to be taken as per the minimum wages applicable in Delhi.
The Income of deceased is being taken as per the minimum wages applicable to a skilled worker applicable in Delhi on the date of accident i.e. Rs. 19,473/- per month.
APPLICATION OF MULTIPLIER:
19.
The age of deceased was around 52 years at the time of accident.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari &
Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Married Persons Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six) Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Bachelor In case family is not large Half

The offending vehicle was registered in the name of R2.
It is not the plea of respondents that accident took place due to involvement of any other vehicle.
R1 did not choose to appear before the Tribunal.
He did not enter into witness box to lead any evidence in his defence.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, 1/3rd of the income of deceased has to be deducted towards his Jyoti Verma vs Pradeep Kumar on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157115972/
9 personal and living expenses.
24. Thus, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs.18,84,986/- (19,473x 2/3 x 110/100 x 12 x 11).
In case of Pranay Sethi (supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-, 18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
In this case, there were three legal heirs of the deceased at the time of accident and filing of the claim petition, being wife and sons.
Thus, claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- (48,000x3+18,000+18,000) under this head.
26. Considering the aforementioned factors, the total compensation is calculated as under:
 S. No. Head Amount  Awarded  1. Monthly income of deceased (A) Rs.19,473/-
 2. Add future prospect (B) @ 10% of 19,473  = 1947.3 3.
Less 1/3 towards personal and living Rs.7140.1/- = expenses of the deceased (C) 1/3rd of 21,420.3(19,47 3+1947.3)
4. Monthly loss of dependency (A+B)-C=D Rs.14,280.2 5.
11. Compensation for funeral expenses (K) Rs.18,000/-
12.
Total compensation Rs. 20,64,986.4 rounded off to Rs.20,65,000/-
27.
Considering that as discussed above, the deceased was himself was also responsible for the accident to some extent and negligent, 10% of compensation is to be deducted towards contributory negligence.
Thus, all the petitioners i.e. wife and children of the deceased in the instant case shall be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.18,58,500/- after deducting 10% of the award amount i.e.
20,65,000/-{20,65,000-2,06,500 (10% of 20,65,000/- comes to Rs.2,06,500/-) } INTEREST ON AWARD 28.
Petitioners shall also be entitled to interest @ 7.5% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization, except for the period for which the interest, if any, has been stopped by order of the Tribunal during inquiry.
LIABILITY 29.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and,
in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance p o l i c y w a s b r e a c h e d / v i o l a t e d b y i n s u r e d , t h e r e f o r e , r e s p o n d e n t n o .
30. In view of above discussion, respondent No. 3/ insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
RELIEF 31.
This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.18,58,500/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs Fifty Eight Thousands Five Hundred Only) to the petitioners along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by the respondent no.3/The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.
32. The apportionment of the award amount shall be decided only after deposit of award amount.
33. With these observations, the claim petition is disposed of.
